extracted.intended_audience: media covering NBA officiating; teams, referees, and NBA officiating staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official NBA guidance on officiating rules, Replay Center procedures, points of education, and bench behavior for the 2022-23 season — intended as a media/reference guide and operational directive for referees and league staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition take foul (definition and identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: New Rule: Impose a heightened penalty when the defense commits a transition take foul — a foul in which the defender does not make a play on the ball to stop a transition scoring opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying a Take Foul: • Primary Factor - Defender does not make a legitimate play on the ball. • Other Common Factors - Defender 'gives up' on the play (e.g., wraps up or grabs opponent). • Defender is out of position and unable to make a legal play on the ball. Rationale: 1) Reduce game stoppages caused by an unaesthetic non-basketball play 2) Increase the number of exciting fast-break opportunities. Proof of Concept: The proposed rule has virtually eliminated transition take fouls in the G League.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition take foul (heightened penalty, exceptions, clarifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Heightened penalty for committing a take foul to stop a transition scoring opportunity: the offensive team is awarded one free throw (which may be attempted by any player on the offensive team in the game at the time of the foul) and retains possession; the defensive player is assessed a common personal foul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions & Clarifications: • Teams may commit a take foul during the last two minutes of the fourth quarter and the last two minutes of any overtime period without triggering the heightened penalty (to allow the defensive tactic of taking a foul to stop the clock). • A take foul committed immediately after a change of possession but before the offense has the opportunity to advance the ball is subject to the heightened penalty. • A foul on any offensive player (including a player who does not have the ball) can satisfy the transition take foul if other elements are met. • Rule does not apply if the offensive player is fouled in the act of shooting (that is a shooting foul). • Any foul committed by a defender attempting to make a legitimate play on the ball remains a common personal foul; the defender may still be assessed a clear-path-to-the-basket foul if criteria for that call are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replay review of out-of-bounds violations (initiation and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The experimental rule regarding replay review of out-of-bounds violations used in 2021-22 has been adopted full-time with specified initiation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this rule: 1) Game officials no longer can initiate replay review of out-of-bounds violations during the last two minutes of the fourth quarter (and the last two minutes of any overtime period). 2) Teams may trigger replay review of out-of-bounds violations via a Coach’s Challenge throughout the entire game. Coach’s Challenge is the only mechanism capable of initiating replay review of out-of-bounds violations at any point during the game.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption of play after Coach's Challenge or inadvertent whistle
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable in connection with a Coach’s Challenge or any call treated as an inadvertent whistle, possession will be awarded to the team that clearly and conclusively would have imminently gained possession at the time of the whistle; if that standard is not met, play resumes via a jump ball.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two factors relevant to determining whether a team clearly and conclusively would have imminently gained possession: 1) The proximity of opposing player(s) to the ball (or lack thereof); and 2) The actual outcome of the play in the natural and immediate aftermath of the whistle (e.g., a player secured the ball).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced instant replay procedure for earlier notice of scoring changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to provide earlier notice of a scoring change resulting from the Replay Center’s review of a made basket that was incorrectly scored during live action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure steps: 1) During live action, Replay Center reviews a made basket to determine if it was incorrectly scored by on-court officials. 2) Replay Center informs the courtside administrator. 3) The courtside administrator turns on a new blue light located at the scorer’s table. 4) Upon noticing the blue light, the on-court officials stop the game at the next neutral opportunity to enable the scoring change to be announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team bench behavior rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules intended to reduce disruptions and distractions during live play by team benches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goal: Reduce disruptions and distractions during live play. Policy Rationale: 1) Integrity of competition 2) Safety of game participants. Rules: • Prolonged standing: Players not in the game may not remain standing at or away from their team’s bench during the game. • Unsportsmanlike distractions: Players and coaches are prohibited from attempting to distract their opponents in an unsportsmanlike manner. Penalties: Violators are subject to in-game penalties (e.g., technical foul, delay of game) and post-game penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of Education topics for officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated instructional emphasis areas for officials during the season as part of Points of Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed topics: Enhanced Instant Replay Procedure, Non-Basketball Moves, Traveling, Freedom of Movement, Respect for the Game. For more on this season’s Points of Education, visit NBA Official at official.nba.com.
